_notes: Source of truth for the v1 consent and privacy UI strings. The two consents[].text values are versioned legal texts: never edit them after launch; a change = a new version row in wcxb_consent_texts.
text_sha256 = lowercase hex sha256 of the exact UTF-8 bytes of text (no trailing newline, no HTML). The consent texts are plain ASCII on purpose so the hash is stable.
The consent texts contain NO placeholders, so one text and one hash fit every plugin. Other strings may use {named} placeholders, filled by the client.
Placeholders used outside the consent texts: {plugin_name}, {email}, {date}, {privacy_url}, {privacy_email}, {confirm_link}, {postal_address}.
D25: no admin email is collected under the usage box in v1. There is no security purpose.

The usage label is NOT 'anonymous' (02-client-protocol.md section 3 says 'Share anonymous usage data'; this file wins). The payload has the site address and a site id, so it is personal data (GDPR Art 4(1), Recital 26). Calling it anonymous would be misleading.
The usage text lists every snapshot field group in 02 section 4.3. If the client starts sending a new field group, ship a new usage text version in the same release.

card.sender_line MUST be shown on the card under the boxes: CASL request-for-consent rules (CRTC Regulations SOR/2012-36 s.4) want the business name, a mailing address and a web or email contact in the request itself. It is kept out of the hashed text so the hash does not depend on the address.
No dark patterns: both boxes unticked; Save and No thanks are the same size and style; no countdown, no guilt text; No thanks is never asked again; Save with no box ticked = No thanks.

Translations: v1 shows the two consent texts in English only (do not wrap them in __()). A translated text needs its own version and hash, for example usage-2026-11-fr. Other UI strings may be translated.
tests/contract/fixtures/*.json use placeholder hashes (ad42..., 04ca...). Replace them with the two text_sha256 values below when the client is built.

consents.text: Share usage data with WPCreatix (Wuzzify LLC, Cairo, Egypt) to help us improve our plugins. This choice covers all WPCreatix plugins on this site. When you click Save, then about once a week, and when one of our plugins is activated, deactivated, updated or deleted, we send: your site address, a random site id, WordPress, PHP and MySQL versions, server type, site language, theme, whether it is a live or test site, whether it is a multisite, which of our plugins you have (version, active or not, install date), your store currency and country if you use WooCommerce, whether some well-known plugins are active (from a fixed list), and rounded counts (for example 100-999 posts, or how often you use some of our features). We also see your country from your server's IP address; we do not store the IP. We never send your content, customer or order data, user names, emails or passwords. You can turn this off at any time in the plugin settings.

Email me news, tips and offers about WPCreatix plugins, sent by WPCreatix (Wuzzify LLC, Cairo, Egypt). We use your email address, and your first name if you give it, only for these emails. We will first send you an email to confirm. You can unsubscribe at any time with the link in every email or in the plugin settings.

We also see your country from your server's IP address; we do not store the IP. If you share usage data, the answer is linked to this site.

_notes: Plain text. No promotion, no tracking pixel, no images, no link tracking: it is a confirmation, not a news email.

FluentCRM 3.2.6 (checked): put #activate_link# where {confirm_link} is (SettingsController.php:151 help text; DoubleOptinRenderer.php:36 replaces it). {postal_address} can be {{crm.business_address}} (ShortcodeParser.php:554) once the FluentCRM business address is set.
From confirm@wpcreatix.com, Reply-To {privacy_email} (D10). On Zoho cap overflow it goes out from the bulk sender (05); the text is the same.

CASL: a message that asks to confirm consent is itself a commercial message (CASL s.1(3)), so it carries the sender name, mailing address, a contact and a way to say no (reply). The person already gave express consent on the card.

Gmail/Yahoo sender rules: wpcreatix.com needs SPF, DKIM and DMARC aligned for the confirm@ From (all senders must authenticate). No List-Unsubscribe is needed on a one-to-one confirmation (verify against the live Google bulk-sender FAQ before launch).
The 30-day line matches D28.

doi_email.confirmed_page_message: Thanks, your email is confirmed. You can unsubscribe at any time with the link in any of our emails.

_notes: FluentCRM campaign footer for news emails (not asked by D-items, needed by CAN-SPAM 15 U.S.C. 7704(a)(5) and CASL s.6(2)). {{crm.unsubscribe_url}} plus the RFC 8058 one-click header FluentCRM adds (05).
